title: A Voice Memo About a Chaotic Morning
script: Narrator: [breathless] Okay, recording this while I walk to the bus stop, because I need to laugh about this later.
Narrator: My alarm didn't go off. Or maybe it did, and I just didn't hear it, I honestly don't know.
Narrator: I woke up twenty minutes late, which doesn't sound bad, but my whole morning runs on a tight schedule.
Narrator: [frustrated] I went to make coffee, and there were no clean mugs. Every single one was in the sink from the weekend.
Narrator: [laughing] So I drank coffee from a small bowl. A bowl. I looked completely ridiculous standing in my kitchen.
Narrator: Then I couldn't find my keys anywhere. I checked my bag, the counter, my coat pocket, nothing.
Narrator: [surprised] They were in the fridge. I still don't understand how that happened, but there they were, next to the milk.
Narrator: At that point I just started laughing, because clearly today was going to be one of those mornings.
Narrator: I grabbed my bag, forgot my lunch on the counter, and only realized it once I was already outside.
Narrator: [resigned] I decided not to go back for it. Some mornings you just have to accept the chaos and keep moving.
Narrator: I bought a sandwich near the office instead. Not ideal for my budget, but honestly, not a disaster either.
Narrator: Walking to the bus stop now, I'm actually starting to feel calmer. The panic always fades once I'm moving.
Narrator: I think mornings like this happen when I don't prepare anything the night before, not even my clothes.
Narrator: [determined] Tonight, I'm going to wash the mugs, find my keys a proper spot, and pack my lunch before bed.
Narrator: I say that every time, though. Let's see if tonight is actually different from all the other times.
Narrator: [relieved] Anyway, the bus is here. Recording this made me feel a little less frazzled, so that's something.
Narrator: Talk later. Hopefully with a calmer story than a bowl of coffee and keys in the fridge.
